title: Correct potential energy
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the gravitational potential energy of ball A as 24 J using the given masses, height, and g.

title: Correct final velocity
description: Essential: Student correctly determines the magnitude of the velocities of A and B when they reach the same height as 2 m/s.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important: Student applies the principle of conservation of mechanical energy to the two-ball system, accounting for changes in potential and kinetic energy.

title: Height change analysis
description: Important: Student correctly identifies that each ball moves a vertical distance of h/2 (0.6 m) to reach the same height.

title: System kinetic energy
description: Important: Student correctly expresses the total kinetic energy as (1/2)(m_A + m_B)v^2, recognizing both masses move with the same speed magnitude.

title: Sign error in energy
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error in the potential energy change, incorrectly adding instead of subtracting the energy changes for A and B.

title: Unit omission or mismatch
description: Pitfall: Student provides numerical answers without correct units (J for energy, m/s for velocity) or uses inconsistent units.

title: Alternative approach
description: Optional: Student solves part (2) using Newton's second law and kinematics (finding acceleration and then velocity) instead of energy conservation.
